deep.reconstruction:
Folio 85r is almost blank. It contains only two fragments, both drafts belonging to the dissertation 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse' (1851), Art. 21.

(1) Top left, upright: a line-ending fragment, probably 'Begrenzungspunkt entspricht'. It continues the sentence at the foot of the previous page: '... die Aufgabe, zwei gegebene Flächen so auf einander zu beziehen, daß jedem Begrenzungspunkte ein [Begrenzungspunkt] entspricht.' This is the geometric form of the conformal-mapping problem. A simply connected surface T is to be mapped one-to-one and conformally onto another surface (in the published text, the unit disk), with boundary going to boundary.

(2) Bottom of the page, written upside down: a two-line note. It reads roughly: 'Nehmen wir nun die complexe Function x+yi von x, y u. setzt Ω = log(z−z'), [entsprechend?] ... dann wird z' durch Variation der Lage eines [Punktes?] ...'.

In modern terms this is the start of Riemann's construction in Art. 21. Fix an interior point z' of T. Look for a function ζ(z) mapping T onto |ζ|<1 with ζ(z')=0. Write log ζ = log(z−z') + t(z), where t = α + iβ is holomorphic on T.
- On the boundary one needs |ζ| = 1. This means α = −log|z−z'| there.
- So α is the harmonic function with boundary values −log|z−z'|. Riemann obtains it via the Dirichlet principle; it is equivalent to Green's function g(z,z') = −log|z−z'| − α.
- β is the harmonic conjugate of α, fixed up to an additive constant.
- ζ = (z−z') e^{t} then gives the mapping.

The note itself goes no further than defining Ω = log(z−z'), the logarithmic singularity at z'. It then mentions varying the position of z' (or of a point). This presumably refers to how the mapping depends on the chosen centre, i.e. the three-real-parameter freedom of the map. All steps after the definition of Ω are my contextual reconstruction from the published Art. 21, not text on this page.
errors: No mathematical errors can be assessed: the page carries only a fragmentary definition Ω = log(z−z'), which is correct as the standard logarithmic singularity.

results.what: Use of Ω = log(z−z') as the singular part of the mapping function / Green's function in the conformal mapping of a simply connected surface onto a disk
results.modern_name: Riemann mapping theorem via the Green's function (log ζ = log(z−z') + t)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, Inauguraldissertation 1851, Art. 21 (rigorous proofs later by Schwarz, Neumann, Osgood, Koebe, Carathéodory)

deep.surprise_reason: These are fragmentary drafts of the published dissertation Art. 21 (conformal mapping of a simply connected surface onto the disk using log(z−z')). The content is well known as Riemann's own, and there is nothing new on the page.
